camera.ground_material_projection: orthographic top-down; the runtime Iso ground transform provides the camera

review: The remade forest ground and flora follow the original user reference together with town-master-scene-v3: softened neutral-grey limestone, fine irregular moss joints, olive low cover, cream-white petals and restrained warm wildflowers. Each 724-square ground cell is cropped two pixels inward to exclude adjacent material boundary pixels; materials are opaque, evenly lit top-down textures, and game projection supplies their camera. The new flora has alpha0 surroundings despite the olive blur stored in invisible RGB. Light/dark composites show leaf and petal holes with no wide halo, attached earth plate or external ground shadow. Natural high leaf surfaces, occluded rear stems and the root-crown contact are reviewed visually; no rigid-edge angles are invented for organic clumps. Actual first-game comparison rejected the ground sheet grass panel as wiry yellow moss. grass-v2.png replaces only grass with low short blades and small clover, maintaining uniform light and no baked canopy shadows; paving and earth remain the measured ground.png cells.

flowers_white.review: Ground-contact centre at the converging lower flower stems under the central leaf rosette. Foreground leaves remain beyond the contact; this is not the lowest petal or silhouette pixel.

flowers_warm.review: Shared rooted centre beneath the warm flower stems and grass rosettes. The thin forward blades retain depth below the anchor.

fern.review: Ground contact under the fern petiole crown and overlapping low leaves. Rear stems and forward fronds retain their natural occlusion and spread.

grass.review: Contact under the dense central grass bases and low leaf rosettes. Tall blades do not determine the anchor, and foreground leaves remain visible below it.
